# EXCLUSIVE DISTRIBUTION AGREEMENT

This Exclusive Distribution Agreement (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of January 1, 2024 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between:

**Brightwater Espresso Systems Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Supplier**"); and

**Halvorsen Coffee Distribution LLC**, a New York limited liability company ("**Distributor**").

Supplier and Distributor are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Supplier designs and manufactures commercial espresso machines for the hospitality and food service industries.

B. Distributor is engaged in the business of marketing, selling, installing and servicing commercial coffee equipment to restaurants, hotels, cafés and other food service operators.

C. Supplier wishes to appoint Distributor as its exclusive distributor of the Products in the Territory, and Distributor wishes to accept that appointment, on the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set out below, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

Capitalized terms used in this Agreement have the meanings given below or where first defined in the text.

1.1 "**Products**" means the commercial espresso machines listed in Exhibit A.

1.2 "**Territory**" means New York, New Jersey and Connecticut.

1.3 "**Purchase Order**" means a written order for Products issued by Distributor to Supplier under Section 4.

1.4 "**Customer**" means any end user of Products located in the Territory that purchases or leases Products from Distributor for its own use and not for resale.

1.5 "**Initial Term**" has the meaning given in Section 2.1, and "**Renewal Term**" has the meaning given in Section 2.2. The Initial Term together with any Renewal Term is the "**Term**."

1.6 "**Marks**" means the trademarks, trade names, logos and service marks of Supplier used in connection with the Products, including BRIGHTWATER and the Brightwater wave logo.

1.7 "**Confidential Information**" has the meaning given in Section 11.1.

1.8 "**Business Day**" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or day on which commercial banks in New York, New York are authorized or required to close.

## 2. TERM

2.1 **Initial Term.** This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier in accordance with Section 15, continues until December 31, 2026 (the "**Initial Term**").

2.2 **Renewal Option.** Distributor may renew this Agreement for one additional term of three (3) years (the "**Renewal Term**") by giving Supplier written notice at least 90 days before Initial Term expiry. Notice of renewal must be given in accordance with Section 17. If Distributor does not give timely notice under this Section 2.2, this Agreement will expire at the end of the Initial Term.

2.3 **Terms of Renewal.** The Renewal Term will be on the terms of this Agreement then in effect, except that the prices in Exhibit B may be adjusted under Section 5.2.

## 3. APPOINTMENT

3.1 **Exclusive Appointment.** Subject to the terms of this Agreement, Supplier appoints Distributor as its exclusive distributor of the Products in the Territory during the Term, and Distributor accepts that appointment.

3.2 **Supplier Restrictions.** During the Term, Supplier shall not, directly or indirectly, sell Products to any person in the Territory, or appoint any other distributor, agent or reseller for Products in the Territory, other than through Distributor. Supplier may continue to sell directly to the national accounts listed in Part 2 of Exhibit A, provided that Supplier pays Distributor a service referral fee equal to five percent (5%) of the net invoice price of each such sale delivered into the Territory.

3.3 **Distributor Restrictions.** Distributor shall not actively solicit sales of Products outside the Territory. During the Term, Distributor shall not distribute any commercial espresso machine manufactured by a competitor of Supplier that is substantially similar in function and price point to any Product, without Supplier's prior written consent.

3.4 **Independent Contractors.** The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, franchise, agency or employment relationship between them. Distributor purchases Products for its own account and sets its own resale prices.

## 4. ORDERS

4.1 **Purchase Orders.** Distributor shall order Products by submitting Purchase Orders to Supplier. Each Purchase Order must state the Products, model numbers, quantities, requested delivery date and delivery location.

4.2 **Acceptance.** Supplier shall accept or reject each Purchase Order within five (5) Business Days of receipt. Supplier shall not unreasonably reject any Purchase Order that conforms to this Agreement. A Purchase Order not rejected within that period is deemed accepted.

4.3 **Forecasts.** By the tenth (10th) day of each calendar quarter, Distributor shall provide Supplier with a non-binding rolling forecast of its anticipated Product requirements for the following two (2) quarters.

4.4 **Conflicting Terms.** Any pre-printed or additional terms in a Purchase Order, acknowledgment or invoice have no effect.

## 5. PRICING AND PAYMENT

5.1 **Prices.** Distributor shall pay the prices for Products set out in Exhibit B. Supplier shall invoice upon shipment.

5.2 **Price Adjustments.** Supplier may adjust the prices in Exhibit B once per calendar year, effective January 1, by giving Distributor at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice. No single annual increase may exceed four percent (4%) over the prices then in effect.

5.3 **Payment Terms.** Undisputed invoices are due within thirty (30) days of receipt. Distributor shall notify Supplier in writing of any disputed amount, with reasonable detail, within fifteen (15) days of receipt of the invoice, an

d the Parties shall work in good faith to resolve the dispute.

5.4 **Late Payment.** Overdue undisputed amounts bear interest at the lesser of one percent (1%) per month and the maximum rate permitted by law.

5.5 **Taxes.** Prices exclude sales, use and similar taxes, which Distributor shall pay or for which it shall provide a valid resale exemption certificate.

## 6. DELIVERY

6.1 **Delivery.** Supplier shall deliver Products FCA Supplier's facility in Allentown, Pennsylvania (Incoterms 2020), unless the Purchase Order specifies another delivery location agreed by Supplier.

6.2 **Title and Risk.** Title and risk of loss pass to Distributor upon delivery under Section 6.1.

6.3 **Inspection.** Distributor shall inspect Products within ten (10) Business Days after receipt and shall notify Supplier in writing of any shortage or visible damage within that period. Supplier shall promptly replace or credit nonconforming Products.

## 7. DISTRIBUTOR OBLIGATIONS

7.1 **Promotion.** Distributor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to promote, market and sell the Products throughout the Territory.

7.2 **Installation and Service.** Distributor shall maintain at least two (2) Supplier-certified service technicians in each state within the Territory and shall provide installation, preventive maintenance and warranty repair services to Customers in accordance with Supplier's published service standards.

7.3 **Inventory.** Distributor shall maintain a reasonable inventory of Products sufficient to meet anticipated Customer demand in the Territory.

7.4 **Compliance.** Distributor shall comply with all laws applicable to its resale, installation and servicing of the Products in the Territory.

7.5 **Reports.** Within thirty (30) days after the end of each calendar quarter, Distributor shall provide Supplier with a report of Product sales by model and state for that quarter.

## 8. SUPPLIER OBLIGATIONS

8.1 **Supply.** Supplier shall use commercially reasonable efforts to fill all accepted Purchase Orders by the requested delivery date.

8.2 **Training and Materials.** Supplier shall provide, at no charge, initial and annual technical training for Distributor's service technicians and reasonable quantities of sales literature and marketing materials.

8.3 **Leads.** Supplier shall promptly refer to Distributor all inquiries it receives regarding the purchase of Products in the Territory, other than inquiries from the national accounts identified in Part 2 of Exhibit A.

8.4 **Discontinuation.** Supplier shall give Distributor at least one hundred twenty (120) days' prior written notice before discontinuing any Product, and shall make spare parts for any discontinued Product available to Distributor for at least seven (7) years after discontinuation.

## 9. WARRANTIES

9.1 **Product Warranty.** Supplier warrants to Distributor and to each Customer that the Products will conform to the specifications in Exhibit A and will be free from defects in materials and workmanship for twelve (12) months after installation at the Customer's premises, but no more than eighteen (18) months after delivery to Distributor.

9.2 **Remedy.** Supplier shall, at its option, repair or replace any Product that does not conform to Section 9.1, and shall reimburse Distributor for warranty labor performed by its certified technicians at the rates set out in Exhibit B.

9.3 **Mutual Warranties.** Each Party represents and warrants that it is duly organized and in good standing, has full authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, and that this Agreement is its valid and binding obligation.

9.4 **Disclaimer.** EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS SECTION 9, SUPPLIER MAKES NO OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

## 10. TRADEMARKS

10.1 **License.** Supplier grants Distributor a non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license during the Term to use the Marks in the Territory solely to advertise and sell the Products, in accordance with Supplier's brand guidelines.

10.2 **Ownership.** All rights in the Marks remain with Supplier. Distributor shall not register or use any trademark, trade name or domain name confusingly similar to the Marks.

## 11. CONFIDENTIALITY

11.1 **Definition.** "**Confidential Information**" means all non-public business, technical and financial information disclosed by one Party to the other in connection with this Agreement, including pricing, customer lists and product specifications.

11.2 **Obligations.** The receiving Party shall use the disclosing Party's Confidential Information only to perform this Agreement and shall not disclose it to any third party other than its employees, advisors and financing sources who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Section 11.

11.3 **Exceptions.** Section 11.2 does not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving Party, was lawfully known to the receiving Party before disclosure, is independently developed, or is required to be disclosed by law, provided the receiving Party gives prompt notice where lawful.

11.4 **Survival.** The obligations in this Section 11 survive for three (3) years after the end of the Term.

## 12. INDEMNIFICATION

12.1 **By Supplier.** Supplier shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Distributor and its members, managers, officers and employees from third-party claims arising out of (a) any defect in the design or manufacture of the Products, (b) any claim that the Products or the Marks infringe the intellectual property rights of a third party, or (c) Supplier's breach of this Agreement.

12.2 **By Distributor.** Distributor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Supplier and its directors, officers and employees from third-party claims arising out of (a) Distributor's negligent installation or servicing of Products, (b) any warranty

or representation regarding the Products made by Distributor beyond those in Section 9, or (c) Distributor's breach of this Agreement.

12.3 **Procedure.** The indemnified Party shall give prompt written notice of any claim, allow the indemnifying Party to control the defense and settlement, and reasonably cooperate at the indemnifying Party's expense. The indemnifying Party shall not settle any claim that imposes obligations on the indemnified Party without its consent.

## 13. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

13.1 EXCEPT FOR OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTIONS 11 AND 12, NEITHER PARTY IS LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR LOST PROFITS, ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT.

13.2 Supplier maintains, and shall continue to maintain during the Term, product liability insurance with limits of not less than $5,000,000 per occurrence, naming Distributor as an additional insured.

## 14. ASSIGNMENT

14.1 **General.** Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations under it, whether voluntarily, by operation of law or otherwise, without the other Party's prior written consent. Supplier may, however, assign this Agreement without consent to a successor to all or substantially all of its espresso machine business that assumes Supplier's obligations in writing.

14.2 **Change of Control of Distributor.** Any transfer, in one transaction or a series of related transactions, of more than fifty percent (50%) of the equity or membership interests in Distributor, or of the power to direct its management and policies, whether by sale, merger, conversion or otherwise, is deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Distributor and requires Supplier's prior written consent. Distributor shall request that consent in writing at least thirty (30) days before the proposed transfer.

14.3 **Void Transfers.** Any purported assignment or transfer in violation of this Section 14 is void.

## 15. TERMINATION

15.1 **Material Breach.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing it, or within ten (10) days in the case of non-payment of undisputed amounts.

15.2 **Insolvency.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if the other Party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or becomes the subject of any voluntary or involuntary bankruptcy proceeding that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days.

15.3 **Unauthorized Assignment or Change of Control.** Supplier may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if Distributor assigns or purports to assign this Agreement, or undergoes a transfer described in Section 14.2, without Supplier's prior written consent.

## 16. EFFECT OF TERMINATION OR EXPIRATION

16.1 **Outstanding Orders.** Upon expiration or termination, Supplier shall fill all Purchase Orders accepted before the effective date of termination, unless Supplier terminated under Section 15.1 for non-payment or under Section 15.2.

16.2 **Repurchase of Inventory.** Within sixty (60) days after expiration or termination other than by Supplier under Sections 15.1, 15.2 or 15.3, Supplier shall repurchase, at Distributor's option, all new, unused and resalable Products in Distributor's inventory at Distributor's net landed cost.

16.3 **Wind-Down.** Distributor may continue to sell Products remaining in its inventory, and to perform warranty and service work for existing Customers, for one hundred eighty (180) days after expiration or termination.

16.4 **Survival.** Sections 9, 11, 12, 13, 16, 17, 18 and 19 survive any expiration or termination of this Agreement.

## 17. NOTICES

17.1 All notices under this Agreement must be in writing and are effective when delivered personally, one (1) Business Day after dispatch by a nationally recognized overnight courier, or three (3) Business Days after mailing by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the following addresses (or other addresses a Party designates by notice):

**If to Supplier:**
Brightwater Espresso Systems Inc.
2200 Industrial Parkway
Allentown, Pennsylvania 18109
Attention: General Counsel

**If to Distributor:**
Halvorsen Coffee Distribution LLC
415 Commerce Drive
Long Island City, New York 11101
Attention: Managing Member

17.2 A copy of any notice sent by email does not by itself constitute notice under this Section 17.

## 18. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTES

18.1 **Governing Law.** This Agreement is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws principles that would require the application of the laws of another jurisdiction.

18.2 **Jurisdiction.** Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement.

18.3 **Waiver of Jury Trial.** EACH PARTY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO A JURY TRIAL IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.

18.4 **Equitable Relief.** A breach of Section 10 or Section 11 may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages are inadequate, and the non-breaching Party may seek injunctive relief without posting a bond.

## 19. MISCELLANEOUS

19.1 **Amendments; Waivers.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties. No waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving Party, and no failure or delay in exercising any right operates as a waiver of it.

19.2 **Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict or inconsistency among the documents comprising this Agreement, the following order of precedence applies: Amendment No. 1, then the Agreement body, then the Exhibits.

19.3 **Force Majeure.** Neither Party is liable for any delay or failure to perform

19.4 **Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force, and the invalid provision will be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable.

19.5 **Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument.

19.6 **Headings.** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

# AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO EXCLUSIVE DISTRIBUTION AGREEMENT

This Amendment No. 1 to Exclusive Distribution Agreement (this "**Amendment No. 1**") is entered into as of March 1, 2025 (the "**Amendment Effective Date**") by and between:

**Brightwater Espresso Systems Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Supplier**"); and

**Halvorsen Coffee Distribution LLC**, a New York limited liability company ("**Distributor**").

Supplier and Distributor are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Supplier and Distributor are parties to an Exclusive Distribution Agreement dated as of January 1, 2024 (the "**Agreement**"). Under the Agreement, Supplier appointed Distributor as its exclusive distributor of the Products in the Territory.

B. The Agreement does not contain a minimum purchase requirement. In consideration of the continuation of Distributor's exclusive appointment under Section 3.1 of the Agreement, the Parties wish to establish an annual minimum purchase commitment and related reporting and remedy provisions.

C. Section 19.1 of the Agreement permits the Agreement to be amended by a written instrument signed by both Parties.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set out below, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 **Defined Terms.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Amendment No. 1 have the meanings given to them in the Agreement.

1.2 **Contract Year.** "**Contract Year**" means each calendar year during the Term, beginning with the calendar year commencing January 1, 2025. If the Term ends on a date other than December 31, the final Contract Year is the period from January 1 of that year to the last day of the Term.

1.3 **Net Purchases.** "**Net Purchases**" means the aggregate net invoice price paid or payable by Distributor to Supplier for goods shipped to Distributor during a Contract Year under accepted Purchase Orders. Net Purchases exclude taxes, freight and insurance charges, credits for returned or nonconforming goods, and any amounts credited or reimbursed under Sections 6.3 or 9.2 of the Agreement.

1.4 **References.** On and after the Amendment Effective Date, each reference in the Agreement to "this Agreement," "hereunder" or words of similar import means the Agreement as amended by this Amendment No. 1.

## 2. RECITALS AND APPOINTMENT

2.1 **Confirmation of Appointment.** Supplier confirms that Distributor's exclusive appointment under Section 3.1 of the Agreement continues in full force, subject to Distributor's satisfaction of the Annual Minimum as provided in Section 3 of this Amendment No. 1.

2.2 **No Change to Territory.** The Territory remains New York, New Jersey and Connecticut.

## 3. ANNUAL MINIMUM PURCHASE COMMITMENT

3.1 **Annual Minimum.** For each Contract Year, Distributor shall make Net Purchases of Products from Supplier of not less than $2,400,000 (the "**Annual Minimum**"). For purposes of this Section 3, Section 4 and Section 5 of this Amendment No. 1, "**Products**" means all goods offered by Supplier from time to time, including spare parts and accessories, whether or not listed in Exhibit A to the Agreement.

3.2 **Proration.** If a Contract Year is shorter than twelve (12) months, the Annual Minimum for that Contract Year will be reduced pro rata based on the number of days in that Contract Year.

3.3 **Supplier Failure to Supply.** The Annual Minimum for a Contract Year will be reduced by the net invoice price of any goods ordered under a Purchase Order that conforms to the Agreement and that Supplier (a) rejects in breach of Section 4.2 of the Agreement, or (b) fails to deliver within sixty (60) days after the requested delivery date, other than because of a force majeure event affecting Supplier under Section 19.3 of the Agreement.

3.4 **No Carryover.** Net Purchases in excess of the Annual Minimum in any Contract Year do not carry over to, and may not be credited against, the Annual Minimum for any other Contract Year.

## 4. REPORTING AND RECONCILIATION

4.1 **Quarterly Statement.** Together with each quarterly report delivered under Section 7.5 of the Agreement, Distributor shall provide Supplier with a statement of its cumulative Net Purchases of Products for the then-current Contract Year.

4.2 **Annual Reconciliation.** Within forty-five (45) days after the end of each Contract Year, Supplier shall deliver to Distributor a written reconciliation showing Distributor's total Net Purchases of Products for that Contract Year, any adjustment under Section 3.2 or Section 3.3, and the amount of any shortfall against the Annual Minimum (a "**Shortfall**"). Distributor may dispute the reconciliation by written notice, with reasonable detail, within thirty (30) days after receipt, and the Parties shall work in good faith to resolve the dispute.

## 5. CONSEQUENCES OF SHORTFALL

5.1 **Cure Period.** If a Shortfall is finally determined under Section 4.2, Distributor may cure the Shortfall by placing Purchase Orders for Products, in addition to its ordinary requirements, with an aggregate net invoice price at least equal to the Shortfall within ninety (90) days after that determination (the "**Cure Period**"). Purchases made to cure a Shortfall do not count toward the Annual Minimum for the Contract Year in which they are made.

5.2 **Conversion to Non-Exclusive.** If Distributor does not cure a Shortfall within the Cure Period, Supplier may, by written notice given within sixty (60) days after the end of the Cure Period, convert Distributor's appointment under Section 3.1 of the Agreement to a non-exclusive appointment, effective thirty (30) days after the notice. Upon that conversion, Section 3.2 and the second sentence of Section 3.3 of the Agreement will cease to apply.

5.3 **Termination.** If a Shortfall exceeding twenty-five percent (25%) of the Annual Min

imum occurs in any Contract Year and is not cured within the Cure Period, or if an uncured Shortfall occurs in two (2) consecutive Contract Years, the failure constitutes a material breach of the Agreement that is not capable of further cure. Supplier may then terminate the Agreement by written notice under Section 15.1 of the Agreement without any additional cure period.

5.4 **Repurchase.** A termination by Supplier under Section 5.3 of this Amendment No. 1 is a termination by Supplier under Section 15.1 of the Agreement for purposes of Sections 16.1 and 16.2 of the Agreement.

5.5 **Exclusive Remedies.** The remedies in this Section 5 are Supplier's sole and exclusive remedies for Distributor's failure to meet the Annual Minimum.

## 6. MISCELLANEOUS

6.1 **Effect of Amendment.** Except as expressly modified by this Amendment No. 1, the Agreement remains unchanged and in full force and effect. The Parties ratify and confirm the Agreement as amended by this Amendment No. 1.

6.2 **Representations.** Each Party represents and warrants that it has full authority to enter into and perform this Amendment No. 1, and that this Amendment No. 1 has been duly authorized, executed and delivered by it and is its valid and binding obligation.

6.3 **Governing Law.** This Amendment No. 1 is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws principles that would require the application of the laws of another jurisdiction. Sections 18.2 and 18.3 of the Agreement apply to this Amendment No. 1.

6.4 **Counterparts.** This Amendment No. 1 may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument.

6.5 **Headings.** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

**Re: Proposed Acquisition of Halvorsen Coffee Distribution LLC**

Dear Mr. Halvorsen:

This letter of intent (this "**Letter**") sets out the principal terms on which Corvane Hospitality Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Buyer**"), proposes to acquire Halvorsen Coffee Distribution LLC, a New York limited liability company (the "**Company**"), from the holders of its membership interests (each a "**Seller**" and together the "**Sellers**"). Buyer, the Company and the Sellers are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

Except as provided in Section 12, this Letter is a non-binding expression of the Parties' present intentions. It creates no legally binding obligation to complete the transaction described in it (the "**Transaction**").

## 1. Transaction Structure

1.1 **Purchase of Interests.** At the Closing (defined in Section 4), Buyer will purchase from the Sellers, and the Sellers will sell to Buyer, 100% of the membership interests in the Company (the "**Interests**"). The Interests will be free and clear of all liens, pledges, options and other encumbrances.

1.2 **Effect.** As a result of the Transaction, the Company will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Buyer. The Company will continue as a separate legal entity, and its contracts, licenses, permits, customer relationships and other assets will remain with the Company.

1.3 **Business.** The Company's business includes the marketing, sale, installation and servicing of commercial coffee equipment to food service operators in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut. This business includes its distribution of Brightwater commercial espresso machines under the Exclusive Distribution Agreement dated as of January 1, 2024 between Brightwater Espresso Systems Inc. and the Company, as amended by Amendment No. 1 dated as of March 1, 2025 (as amended, the "**Distribution Agreement**") (the "**Business**").

## 2. Purchase Price

2.1 **Base Price.** The aggregate purchase price for the Interests will be $18,500,000 (the "**Base Price**"). The Base Price assumes the Company will be delivered on a cash-free, debt-free basis with a normalized level of net working capital.

# WAREHOUSE SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Warehouse Services Agreement (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of June 1, 2025 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between:

**Tidemark Logistics LLC**, a New Jersey limited liability company ("**Warehouse Provider**"); and

**Halvorsen Coffee Distribution LLC**, a New York limited liability company ("**Customer**").

Warehouse Provider and Customer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Warehouse Provider operates a public and contract warehouse facility located at 600 Meadowlands Parkway, Secaucus, New Jersey 07094 (the "**Facility**").

B. Customer markets, sells, installs and services commercial coffee equipment, and wishes to engage Warehouse Provider to receive, store, handle and release its inventory at the Facility.

C. Warehouse Provider wishes to provide those services on the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set out below, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

Capitalized terms used in this Agreement have the meanings given below or where first defined in the text.

1.1 "**Goods**" means the commercial coffee equipment, spare parts, accessories, packaging and related merchandise that Customer tenders to Warehouse Provider for storage at the Facility, as identified in Warehouse Receipts.

1.2 "**Services**" means the receiving, storage, handling, inventory control, order picking, packing, loading and related services described in Section 3 and Exhibit A.

1.3 "**Warehouse Receipt**" means the non-negotiable warehouse receipt or electronic receiving record issued by Warehouse Provider under Section 4.2 for Goods received at the Facility.

1.4 "**Release Order**" means a written or electronic instruction from Customer to Warehouse Provider to release, pick, pack or ship specified Goods.

1.5 "**Business Day**" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or day on which commercial banks in New York, New York are authorized or required to close.

1.6 "**WMS**" means Warehouse Provider's web-based warehouse management system, through which Customer may submit Release Orders and view inventory records.

## 2. TERM

2.1 **Initial Term.** This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier in accordance with Section 13, continues until May 31, 2028 (the "**Initial Term**").

2.2 **Automatic Renewal.** After the Initial Term, this Agreement renews automatically for successive one (1) year periods (each a "**Renewal Period**") unless either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days before the end of the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Period.

2.3 **Rates on Renewal.** Warehouse Provider may adjust the rates in Exhibit B effective at the start of any Renewal Period by giving Customer at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice. No adjustment may exceed five percent (5%) over the rates then in effect.

## 3. SERVICES

3.1 **Scope.** Warehouse Provider shall perform the Services at the Facility in a good and workmanlike manner, in accordance with this Agreement, the operating procedures in Exhibit A and generally accepted standards of the warehousing industry in the New York metropolitan area.

3.2 **Dedicated Space.** Warehouse Provider shall make available to Customer not less than 12,000 square feet of dry, enclosed, racked storage space within the Facility (the "**Dedicated Space**"), together with shared access to dock doors and staging areas. Customer may request additional space on thirty (30) days' notice, subject to availability, at the rates in Exhibit B.

3.3 **Hours.** Warehouse Provider shall receive and release Goods between 7:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Business Days. Services outside those hours are available on twenty-four (24) hours' notice at the after-hours rates in Exhibit B.

3.4 **Order Fulfillment.** Warehouse Provider shall pick, pack and stage for carrier pickup all Goods covered by a Release Order received by 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time on a Business Day by the close of that Business Day, and all other Release Orders by the close of the following Business Day.

3.5 **Personnel.** Warehouse Provider shall furnish all labor, supervision, material handling equipment and racking necessary to perform the Services. All personnel performing the Services are employees or subcontractors of Warehouse Provider, and Warehouse Provider is solely responsible for their wages, benefits, withholdings and supervision.

3.6 **Independent Contractor.** Warehouse Provider is an independent contractor. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between the Parties.

## 4. RECEIPT AND STORAGE OF GOODS

4.1 **Advance Notice.** Customer shall give Warehouse Provider advance shipping notice, by WMS or email, of each inbound shipment at least one (1) Business Day before its scheduled arrival, stating the carrier, number of units, model or part numbers and any special handling requirements.

4.2 **Receiving.** Warehouse Provider shall unload, count and visually inspect each inbound shipment upon arrival and shall issue a Warehouse Receipt within one (1) Business Day. Warehouse Provider shall note on the carrier's delivery receipt, and report to Customer within one (1) Business Day, any shortage, overage or visible damage. Warehouse Receipts are non-negotiable and are issued solely in the name of Customer.

4.3 **Storage Conditions.** Warehouse Provider shall store Goods in the Dedicated Space in a clean, dry, secure and climate-moderated environment, maintained between 40°F and 95°F, and shall follow the stacking and orientation markings on Goods packaging.

4.4 **Segregation.** Warehouse Provider shall keep Goods physically segregated from goods of other customers and identified as Customer's prop

5.1 **Records.** Warehouse Provider shall maintain accurate, real-time inventory records of all Goods in the WMS, by stock-keeping unit and serial number where applicable, and shall give Customer continuous read-only access to those records.

Customer is responsible for selecting carriers and paying freight charges unless Customer requests that Warehouse Provider arrange freight, in which case Warehouse Provider shall invoice freight at cost plus the handling fee in Exhibit B.

9.2 **Limit.** Warehouse Provider's liability for loss of or damage to Goods is limited to Customer's documented landed cost of the affected Goods, up to a maximum of $250,000 per occurrence and $1,000,000 in the aggregate in any calendar year. Customer may increase these limits for specified Goods by written request and payment of the additional valuation charge in Exhibit B.

9.3 **Exclusions.** Warehouse Provider is not liable for loss or damage caused by (a) concealed damage or defects in Goods existing before receipt, (b) inadequate packaging furnished by Customer or its suppliers, or (c) a force majeure event under Section 16.3, except to the extent Warehouse Provider's negligence contributed to the loss.

9.4 **Claims.** Customer shall give Warehouse Provider written notice of any claim for loss or damage within sixty (60) days after Customer learns of the loss or damage, and in any event within nine (9) months after the Goods are released or reported lost.

Best: (a) commercial general liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence; (b) warehouse legal liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence; (c) workers' compensation insurance as required by law; and (d) automobile liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 combined single limit. Warehouse Provider shall name Customer as an additional insured on the policy in clause (a).

10.2 **Customer Insurance.** Customer is responsible for insuring Goods against first-party property loss at their full value. Customer shall cause its property insurers to waive subrogation against Warehouse Provider except to the extent of Warehouse Provider's liability under Section 9.
